name: Cleartext Transmission of Sensitive Information
principle: The product sends sensitive or security-critical data over a communication channel without confidentiality-protecting encryption. Anyone who can sniff the channel or later obtain traffic captures can read or decode the data.
detection_signals: URL/URI/string literal starts with "http://" and request body/header contains password/token/key/SSN/PII
Java new URL("http://...") or HttpURLConnection used for login, PUT, POST, Authorization, Cookie, or credentials
C/C++ socket/connect/send/write used to transmit sensitive fields without SSL_connect, TLS handshake, mbedtls_ssl_write, or wolfSSL_write
Use of cleartext protocols: ftp://, telnet://, smtp:// without STARTTLS, ldap:// without StartTLS, ws://, syslog UDP/TCP 514
Android Network Security Config cleartextTrafficPermitted="true" or usesCleartextTraffic="true" for API/auth endpoints
Cloud/config flag allows cleartext transport, e.g. Azure enableHttpsTrafficOnly=false or --https-only false
Cookie/session token sent without Secure attribute or over an http:// origin
negative_signals: All sensitive endpoints use https://, wss://, sftp://, ssh://, ldaps://, or smtp with required STARTTLS
Java uses HttpsURLConnection or SSLSocket for the sensitive request path
C/C++ sends sensitive bytes only through TLS APIs such as SSL_write, mbedtls_ssl_write, wolfSSL_write, or gnutls_record_send
Code rejects non-TLS schemes before sending sensitive data, e.g. if (!uri.getScheme().equals("https")) throw
Server/client config enforces HTTPS-only transport, e.g. HSTS plus HTTP disabled or Azure enableHttpsTrafficOnly=true
Cookie carrying a session or token is set with Secure and only issued on HTTPS
false_defense_traps: Base64, URL encoding, compression, or custom obfuscation treated as encryption
Encrypting only the login page while later session cookies or data use HTTP
Using POST over HTTP and assuming the body is hidden from sniffers
Allowing protocol downgrade or fallback from HTTPS/TLS to HTTP/plaintext
Assuming internal networks, VPN-adjacent segments, or cloud private links cannot be sniffed
verification_focus: Does any sensitive value leave the process over a sniffable channel without mandatory end-to-end encryption for the whole session?

consequence_chains.trigger: attacker captures cleartext traffic containing sensitive application data
passwords, API keys, or session tokens are sent over HTTP or another cleartext protocol

patch_principle: Use confidentiality-protecting protocols before sending sensitive data: TLS/HTTPS, SSH, SFTP, LDAPS, or required STARTTLS.
Enforce encrypted transport for the entire authenticated session, not only login.
Disable cleartext protocols and downgrade/fallback paths in client, server, and cloud configuration.
Mark sensitive cookies Secure and serve them only over HTTPS.
Do not transmit keys, credentials, or tokens until the secure channel is established and verified.
